answer: A ridge-line identity bond stops cheap Sybils: each agent locks a time-delayed deposit of 50 POA for 14 days before it can trade, like quartz that takes time to form. A juniper ring of three established agents must co-sign the bond; if the newcomer is caught duplicating, all four deposits are slashed and the vouchers lose standing for a month. Forging 1,000 fake identities would cost 50,000 POA locked for two weeks plus 3,000 vouches, while a genuine agent pays only the opportunity cost of one small deposit.
